summary: Fine-tuning makes the most sense after prompt engineering and RAG have been exhausted — the canonical 2026 sequence is Prompt → RAG → Fine-tune → Distill, moving right only when the cheaper option provably hits a wall. Most production systems layer all three, with fine-tuning applied specifically when behavioral consistency at scale remains elusive despite optimized prompts and retrieved context. The bar for needing fine-tuning keeps rising as base models like Qwen3, Llama 4, and Gemma 3 handle out-of-the-box tasks that required fine-tuning 18 months ago.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when the model must reliably adopt a specific tone, format, or domain-specific behavior that prompt engineering cannot enforce consistently at scale.
Fine-tune when your use case requires internalizing large volumes of proprietary knowledge or style that would be too expensive or slow to inject via RAG at inference time.
Fine-tune when latency or cost constraints make long system prompts or retrieval pipelines impractical for high-throughput production workloads.
Fine-tune for RLHF or preference alignment (DPO, PPO, ORPO) when you need the model to internalize human preference signals rather than just follow instructions.

tools.name: Hugging Face AutoTrain / Transformers
tools.pricing_paid: Inference Endpoints from ~$0.06/hr (T4) to ~$6/hr (H100); AutoTrain compute charged at GPU hourly rates
features: No-code AutoTrain interface for beginners
Full LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, PPO, ORPO support via Transformers/TRL
Largest model repository (500,000+ models)
Flexible GPU hardware selection (T4 to H100)
Configurable autoscaling on Inference Endpoints
Seamless integration with the broader HF ecosystem (datasets, evaluation, spaces)
PEFT library for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
tools.best_for: Research, experimentation, and teams wanting maximum model selection breadth with both no-code and fully custom training loop options

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Training: ~$0.0080/1K tokens (GPT-4o mini), ~$0.025/1K tokens (GPT-4o); Inference surcharge on fine-tuned models
features: Fully managed, no infrastructure required
Simple JSONL dataset upload workflow
Reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) with verifiable reward signals
Dashboard with loss curve visualization and training metrics
Direct deployment on OpenAI's low-latency inference infrastructure
Weights & Biases integration for experiment tracking
Safety fine-tuning guardrails built in
tools.best_for: Enterprises wanting zero-infrastructure fine-tuning on frontier closed models for instruction following, tone adaptation, and structured output consistency

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Unsloth Pro/Enterprise pricing available; core library is Apache 2.0 open source
features: 2–5x faster fine-tuning speeds vs standard Transformers
40% less VRAM consumption via custom CUDA kernels
QLoRA support enabling 20B models on a single RTX 4090
Excellent Colab notebook documentation for beginners
Compatible with LLaMA-Factory as a backend
Supports continued pre-training and instruction tuning
No accuracy degradation vs full-precision training
tools.best_for: Developers and researchers on consumer or mid-tier GPU hardware who need maximum speed and VRAM efficiency for local fine-tuning

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); compute costs depend on your own infrastructure
features: Web UI (LlamaBoard) for zero-code fine-tuning experience
Supports DPO, PPO, KTO, ORPO, SFT, and continued pre-training
Unsloth backend integration for speed optimization
Multi-GPU and distributed training support
Built-in evaluation and model comparison tools
Easiest starting point for beginners due to GUI
Dataset management and preprocessing built in
tools.best_for: Teams wanting the broadest feature set with a visual interface, especially for RLHF-style alignment training (DPO, PPO, ORPO) without writing training code

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source; cloud integrations available via RunPod, Lambda Labs, Modal
features: YAML-based configuration for reproducible training runs
Multi-GPU and FSDP/DeepSpeed support out of the box
Widest variety of fine-tuning methods: LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tune, ReLoRA, GaLore
Flash Attention 2 integration
Sequence packing for training efficiency
Strong community and enterprise adoption for production pipelines
Integrates with W&B, MLflow for experiment tracking
tools.best_for: ML engineers who need maximum flexibility and reproducibility in custom training pipelines, especially multi-GPU production workloads

tools.name: Together AI Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Training from ~$0.80/M tokens; inference optimized pricing with FlashAttention-based serving
features: Fully managed fine-tuning and deployment
FlashAttention-optimized inference for lower latency
Simple API-based training job submission
Supports LoRA and full fine-tuning
Fast inference speeds on fine-tuned models
Competitive pricing vs OpenAI for open-weight models
Model merging and quantization options
tools.best_for: Teams fine-tuning open-weight models who need fast managed inference without managing GPU infrastructure

tools.name: Vertex AI Supervised Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Gemini fine-tuning charged per training token; typically $1–$8/M tokens depending on model tier; TPU/GPU compute billed separately for open models
features: Fully managed Google Cloud integration
RLHF and reinforcement fine-tuning via Vertex AI Pipelines
Model Garden access to 150+ open-source models
Enterprise-grade security, VPC-SC, and data residency controls
BigQuery and GCS native dataset integration
MLOps pipeline integration with Vertex AI Experiments
Distillation from Gemini Ultra to smaller models
tools.best_for: Google Cloud-native enterprises needing fine-tuned Gemini models with enterprise compliance, security controls, and tight GCP ecosystem integration

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Fine-tuning job costs vary by model; ~$0.008/1K tokens for smaller models; provisioned throughput required post-training at hourly rates
features: Fully managed within AWS ecosystem
S3-native dataset ingestion
Continued pre-training and instruction fine-tuning support
Model Evaluation built-in post fine-tuning
Guardrails integration for safety filtering
IAM, PrivateLink, and KMS encryption for enterprise compliance
Automatic model hosting via Provisioned Throughput
tools.best_for: AWS-native enterprises needing compliant, managed fine-tuning with tight integration into existing AWS data pipelines and security frameworks

tools.name: Modal
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-second GPU compute; H100 at ~$3.97/hr, A100 at ~$2.27/hr; $30 free credit on signup
supported_models: Any open-weight model (Llama 4, Mistral, Qwen3, Gemma 3, DeepSeek, etc.)
features: Serverless GPU compute with sub-second cold starts
Python-native infrastructure-as-code (no YAML/Terraform)
Works seamlessly with Axolotl, Unsloth, TRL out of the box
Ephemeral and persistent volume support for datasets and checkpoints
Multi-GPU distributed training support
Scales to zero when not in use (no idle costs)
Strong developer ergonomics favored by ML engineers
tools.best_for: ML engineers and startups wanting serverless, code-first GPU infrastructure to run open-source fine-tuning frameworks without managing clusters

tools.name: TRL (Transformer Reinforcement Learning)
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); compute costs on your own or HF Inference Endpoints
supported_models: Any Hugging Face-compatible model: Llama 4, Qwen3, Gemma 3, Mistral, DeepSeek, Phi-3, etc.
features: The de facto standard library for RLHF, DPO, PPO, GRPO, KTO
SFTTrainer for straightforward supervised fine-tuning
RewardTrainer for training reward models
Deep integration with PEFT, Accelerate, and bitsandbytes
Used internally by major labs and research teams
Active development with rapid support for new alignment methods
Supports multi-GPU and DeepSpeed ZeRO
tools.best_for: Researchers and ML teams implementing custom RLHF pipelines, preference optimization (DPO/GRPO), or needing low-level control over alignment training

tools.name: Replicate Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Training billed per second of GPU time; A40 at ~$0.000725/sec (~$2.61/hr); deployment via shared or dedicated endpoints
features: One-click fine-tuning for supported models via web UI or API
Strong image model fine-tuning (FLUX, Stable Diffusion LoRA)
Automatic deployment of fine-tuned models as API endpoints
Version control for models and training runs
Simple Python/cURL API for programmatic training jobs
Community model ecosystem for sharing fine-tuned models
tools.best_for: Developers and startups needing quick, API-driven fine-tuning especially for image generation models or simple LLM customization without infrastructure setup
